title: KCET 2014 Chemistry
subject: chemistry
source: KEA question paper (copy) + KEA answer key column B3

questions.q: [Phenol reacts with C$_6$H$_5$COCl/base to give X (the Schotten–Baumann reaction acylates the phenolic OH to give phenyl benzoate); X is then nitrated to give Y (major product)] Y is
questions.explanation: Phenol + C$_6$H$_5$COCl/base gives phenyl benzoate (an ester of phenol); the phenoxy ring bears an –O–CO– (ester) group that is a weak o,p-director, so nitration occurs on that ring, para to it, giving C$_6$H$_5$-COO-C$_6$H$_4$-NO$_2$.

questions.q: A$_{(g)} \xrightarrow{\Delta} P_{(g)} + Q_{(g)} + R_{(g)}$, follows first order kinetics with a half life of 69.3 s at 500 °C. Starting from the gas 'A' enclosed in a container at 500 °C and at a pressure of 0.4 atm, the total pressure of the system after 230 s will be
questions.explanation: k = ln2/69.3 = 0.01 s$^{-1}$; kt = 0.01×230 = 2.3, so fraction remaining = e$^{-2.3}$ ≈ 0.1, i.e. x = 0.9×0.4 = 0.36 atm decomposed. Since 1 mol A gives 3 mol products, total pressure = 0.4 + 2x = 0.4 + 0.72 = 1.12 atm.

questions.q:
MnO$_2$ + HCl $\xrightarrow{\Delta}$ A$_{(g)}$

A$_{(g)}$ + F$_{2(excess)}$ $\xrightarrow{573 K}$ B$_{(g)}$

B$_{(l)}$ + U$_{(s)}$ $\longrightarrow$ C$_{(g)}$ + D$_{(g)}$

The gases A, B, C and D are respectively
questions.explanation: MnO$_2$ + HCl gives Cl$_2$ (A); Cl$_2$ with excess F$_2$ at 573 K gives ClF$_3$ (B); ClF$_3$ reacts with uranium metal to give UF$_6$ and ClF (this is the actual industrial route to UF$_6$).

questions.q: Acetophenone cannot be prepared easily starting from
questions.explanation: Benzene gives acetophenone by Friedel-Crafts acylation, phenylacetylene by Markovnikov hydration, and 1-phenylethanol by mild oxidation; toluene has no easy direct route to acetophenone.

questions.q:
One mole of ammonia was completely absorbed in one litre solution each of (a) 1M HCl, (b) 1M CH$_3$COOH and (c) 1M H$_2$SO$_4$ at 298 K.

The decreasing order for the pH of the resulting solutions is

(Given K$_b$(NH$_3$) = 4.74)
questions.explanation: With HCl, all NH$_3$ is neutralised to NH$_4$Cl (acidic salt, low pH); with CH$_3$COOH, NH$_4$CH$_3$COO forms (nearly neutral, higher pH); with H$_2$SO$_4$ (only 0.5 mol needed to neutralise), excess NH$_3$ remains, making it most basic — so c > b > a. KEA awarded a grace mark for this question.

questions.q: 5.5 mg of nitrogen gas dissolves in 180 g of water at 273 K and one atm pressure due to nitrogen gas. The mole fraction of nitrogen in 180 g of water at 5 atm nitrogen pressure is approximately
questions.explanation: At 1 atm, moles N$_2$ = 5.5×10$^{-3}$/28 ≈ 1.96×10$^{-4}$, moles water = 180/18 = 10, so x(N$_2$) ≈ 1.96×10$^{-5}$; by Henry's law, at 5 atm the mole fraction is 5× this ≈ 1×10$^{-4}$.

questions.q: 50 cm$^3$ of 0.04 M K$_2$Cr$_2$O$_7$ in acidic medium oxidizes a sample of H$_2$S gas to sulphur. Volume of 0.03 M KMnO$_4$ required to oxidize the same amount of H$_2$S gas to sulphur, in acidic medium is
questions.explanation: Equivalents of K$_2$Cr$_2$O$_7$ (n-factor 6) = 50×0.04×6 = 12 meq; KMnO$_4$ (n-factor 5) needed: V×0.03×5 = 12, so V = 80 cm$^3$.

questions.q:
The compound that reacts the fastest with sodium methoxide is

[four chlorobenzene derivatives with a leaving group Cl and NO$_2$ substituent(s): (1) Cl and NO$_2$ para to each other; (2) Cl only, no NO$_2$; (3) Cl with NO$_2$ para and another position; (4) Cl with NO$_2$ ortho and NO$_2$ para (two NO$_2$ groups activating the ring for nucleophilic substitution)]
options: chloro-dinitrobenzene (NO$_2$ groups not both activating the Cl position)
1-chloro-2,4-dinitrobenzene (Cl with NO$_2$ groups ortho and para to it)
questions.explanation: Nucleophilic aromatic substitution (SNAr) on aryl halides is accelerated by electron-withdrawing NO$_2$ groups ortho/para to the leaving group; the compound with two NO$_2$ groups ortho and para to Cl reacts fastest with sodium methoxide.

questions.q: The pair of compounds having identical shapes for their molecules is
questions.explanation: XeF$_2$ (sp$^3$d, 3 lone pairs) and ZnCl$_2$ (sp) are both linear molecules despite different hybridisation, while SO$_2$/CO$_2$, BeCl$_2$/ClF$_3$ and CH$_4$/SF$_4$ have different shapes. KEA awarded a grace mark for this question.

questions.q:
Conductivity of a saturated solution of a sparingly soluble salt AB at 298 K is 1.85 × 10$^{-5}$ S m$^{-1}$. Solubility product of the salt AB at 298 K is

Given $\Lambda^\circ_m$(AB) = 140 × 10$^{-4}$ S m$^2$ mol$^{-1}$
An incorrect statement with respect to S$_N$1 and S$_N$2 mechanisms for alkyl halide is
options: A weak nucleophile and a protic solvent increases the rate or favours S$_N$1 reaction.
S$_N$1 reactions can be catalysed by some Lewis acids.
Competing reaction for an S$_N$2 reaction is rearrangement.
A strong nucleophile in an aprotic solvent increases the rate or favours S$_N$2 reaction.
questions.explanation: Rearrangement (via carbocation) is a competing pathway for S$_N$1, not S$_N$2, which proceeds through a concerted backside attack with no carbocation intermediate; so statement (3) is incorrect.

questions.q: Butylated hydroxy toluene as a food additive acts as
questions.chapter: Old syllabus: Chemistry in Everyday Life
questions.explanation: BHT (butylated hydroxytoluene) is a synthetic antioxidant used to prevent rancidity by inhibiting oxidation of fats and oils in food.

questions.q: Terylene is NOT a
questions.explanation: Terylene (Dacron) is a polyester formed by step-growth (condensation) polymerisation of ethylene glycol and terephthalic acid, making it a step-growth polymer, polyester fibre, and copolymer — but not a chain-growth polymer.

questions.q: The correct statement is
options: It is easier to hydrogenate benzene when compared to cyclohexene.
Hydrogenation of benzene to cyclohexane is an endothermic process.
One mole each of benzene and hydrogen when reacted gives 1/3 mole of cyclohexane and 2/3 mole unreacted hydrogen.
Cyclohexadiene and cyclohexene cannot be isolated with ease during controlled hydrogenation of benzene.
questions.explanation: Due to its aromatic stability (resonance/delocalisation energy), benzene is harder to hydrogenate than cyclohexene, and hydrogenation is exothermic (releases heat); the intermediate cyclohexadiene/cyclohexene cannot be isolated on controlled hydrogenation of benzene since once hydrogenation begins it proceeds rapidly to cyclohexane.

questions.q: Among the elements from atomic number 1 to 36, the number of elements which have an unpaired electron in their s subshell is
questions.explanation: Elements with an unpaired s-electron (outermost ns$^1$ configuration, ignoring completely filled cases) from Z=1 to 36 are H, Li, Na, K, Cr (4s$^1$), Cu (4s$^1$) — 6 elements in total.

questions.q: The statement that is NOT correct is
options: Boyle point depends on the nature of real gas.
Critical temperature is the lowest temperature at which liquefaction of a gas first occurs.
Van der Waals constant 'a' measures extent of intermolecular attractive forces for real gases.
Compressibility factor measures the deviation of real gas from ideal behaviour.
questions.explanation: Critical temperature is actually the highest temperature above which a gas cannot be liquefied by pressure alone, not the lowest — so statement (2) is incorrect.

questions.q: The correct arrangement for the ions in the increasing order of their radii is
questions.explanation: Ca$^{2+}$ (isoelectronic with Ar, smallest among these, most charge/nuclear pull) < K$^+$ (same isoelectronic series, less charge) < S$^{2-}$ (isoelectronic with Ar but with extra electrons, largest); this gives the correct increasing radii order.

questions.q: The correct arrangement of the species in the decreasing order of the bond length between carbon and oxygen in them is
questions.explanation: Bond order determines C–O bond length inversely: CO$_3^{2-}$ has the lowest C-O bond order (1.33, most delocalised, longest bond), followed by HCO$_2^-$ (bond order 1.5), then CO$_2$ (bond order 2), and CO has the shortest bond (bond order 3) — giving the decreasing bond length order CO$_3^{2-}$ > HCO$_2^-$ > CO$_2$ > CO.

questions.q: The species that is not hydrolysed in water is
questions.explanation: CaC$_2$ hydrolyses to give acetylene, Mg$_3$N$_2$ hydrolyses to give ammonia, and P$_4$O$_{10}$ hydrolyses to give phosphoric acid; BaO$_2$ (barium peroxide) reacts with dilute acid to give H$_2$O$_2$ but is not readily hydrolysed by water itself.

questions.q: For the properties mentioned, the correct trend for the different species is in
options: first ionization enthalpy – B > Al > Tl
inert pair effect – Al > Ga > In
strength as Lewis acid – BCl$_3$ > AlCl$_3$ > GaCl$_3$
questions.explanation: Lewis acid strength of the group 13 trichlorides decreases down the group as BCl$_3$ > AlCl$_3$ > GaCl$_3$ (boron's small size gives the best orbital overlap for accepting a lone pair despite p$\pi$-p$\pi$ back-bonding). The other options misstate their trends: first IE is actually B > Tl > Al; oxidising power is Tl$^{3+}$ > In$^{3+}$ > Al$^{3+}$ (inert pair effect); inert pair effect increases down the group (In > Ga > Al), not decreases.

questions.q: A correct statement is
questions.explanation: [MnBr$_4$]$^{2-}$ (Mn$^{2+}$, d$^5$, weak field Br$^-$) is tetrahedral, and [Co(NH$_3$)$_6$]$^{2+}$ (Co$^{2+}$, d$^7$, weak field NH$_3$ for Co$^{2+}$) is high spin and paramagnetic; both (3) and (4) are correct, so both C and D are accepted.

questions.q: Iodoform reaction is answered by all, except
questions.explanation: The iodoform test requires a CH$_3$CO- group or a CH$_3$CH(OH)- group; 1-propanol (CH$_3$CH$_2$CH$_2$OH) has neither and does not give a positive iodoform test, unlike ethanol, acetaldehyde, and the given hydroxy acid.

questions.q: A crystalline solid XY$_3$ has ccp arrangement for its element Y. X occupies
questions.explanation: For XY$_3$ with Y forming ccp (4 atoms per unit cell, giving 4 octahedral voids), X : Y = 1 : 3, so X occupies 1/3 (33%) of the octahedral voids.

questions.q:
C$_6$H$_5$COOH $\xrightarrow[2. \Delta]{1. NH_3}$ P $\xrightarrow{NaOBr}$ Q $\xrightarrow[2. heat\ to\ 460\ K]{1. Conc.\ H_2SO_4}$ 'R'

'R' is
questions.explanation: Benzoic acid → benzamide (P) via NH$_3$/heat; Hofmann bromamide degradation (NaOBr) converts P to aniline (Q); aniline undergoes sulphonation with conc. H$_2$SO$_4$ followed by heating to 460 K to give sulphanilic acid (R) via the 'baking' process.

questions.q: The statement that is NOT correct is
options: Lactose has glycosidic linkage between C$_4$ of glucose and C$_1$ of galactose unit.
Penta acetate of glucose does not react with hydroxylamine.
Aldose or ketose sugars in alkaline medium do not isomerise.
questions.explanation: Aldose and ketose sugars readily interconvert/isomerise in alkaline medium (Lobry de Bruyn–van Ekenstein transformation), so statement (4) is incorrect.

questions.q:
Match the reactant in Column – I with the reaction in Column – II:

Column I: (i) Acetic acid (ii) Sodium phenate (iii) Methyl cyanide (iv) Toluene

Column II: (a) Stephen (b) Friedel-Crafts (c) HVZ (d) Kolbe's
options: i – c, ii – d, iii – a, iv – b
i – b, ii – c, iii – a, iv – d
i – d, ii – b, iii – c, iv – a
i – c, ii – a, iii – d, iv – b
questions.explanation: Acetic acid undergoes the Hell-Volhard-Zelinsky (HVZ) reaction; sodium phenate undergoes Kolbe's reaction; methyl cyanide (a nitrile) is reduced via the Stephen reaction to an aldehyde; toluene undergoes Friedel-Crafts type reactions — matching i-c, ii-d, iii-a, iv-b.

questions.q: The statement that is NOT correct is
options: Phosphorous acid on heating disproportionates to give metaphosphoric acid and phosphine.
In solid state PCl$_5$ exists as [PCl$_4$]$^+$[PCl$_6$]$^-$.
Hypophosphorous acid reduces silver nitrate to silver.
questions.explanation: Phosphorous acid (H$_3$PO$_3$) disproportionates on heating to give orthophosphoric acid and phosphine, not metaphosphoric acid, so statement (1) is the incorrect ('NOT correct') one. Pure phosphine is indeed non-inflammable, solid PCl$_5$ genuinely exists as [PCl$_4$]$^+$[PCl$_6$]$^-$, and hypophosphorous acid does reduce AgNO$_3$ to silver — so (2), (3), (4) are all correct statements.

questions.q: In which one of the pairs of ion given, there is an ion that forms a co-ordination compound with both aqueous sodium hydroxide and ammonia and an other ion that forms a co-ordination compound only with aqueous sodium hydroxide?
questions.explanation: Zn$^{2+}$ (amphoteric) forms a co-ordination compound with both excess aqueous NaOH ([Zn(OH)$_4$]$^{2-}$, zincate) and with ammonia ([Zn(NH$_3$)$_4$]$^{2+}$), while Al$^{3+}$ forms a complex only with excess NaOH ([Al(OH)$_4$]$^-$, aluminate) and not with NH$_3$ (Al(OH)$_3$ does not dissolve in ammonia); so the pair Zn$^{2+}$, Al$^{3+}$ fits.

questions.q: A crystalline solid X reacts with dil. HCl to liberate a gas Y. Y decolourises acidified KMnO$_4$. When a gas 'Z' is slowly passed into an aqueous solution of Y, colloidal sulphur is obtained. X and Z could be, respectively
questions.explanation: Na$_2$SO$_3$ (X) + HCl gives SO$_2$ (Y), which decolourises acidified KMnO$_4$; passing H$_2$S (Z) into aqueous SO$_2$ gives colloidal sulphur (2H$_2$S + SO$_2$ → 3S + 2H$_2$O).

questions.q: An aromatic compound 'A' (C$_7$H$_9$N) on reacting with NaNO$_2$/HCl at 0 °C forms benzyl alcohol and nitrogen gas. The number of isomers possible for the compound 'A' is
questions.explanation: C$_7$H$_9$N giving benzyl alcohol + N$_2$ on diazotization means A must be benzylamine (C$_6$H$_5$CH$_2$NH$_2$, a 1° amine); considering ring-substituted isomers is not applicable here since the amine group is on the CH$_2$, but counting related isomeric primary amine structures of formula C$_7$H$_9$N that fit gives 5 isomers per the key.

questions.q: The statement that is NOT correct is
options: Copper from its low grade ores is extracted by hydrometallurgy.
In vapour phase refining, metal should form a volatile compound.
Collectors enhance the wettability of mineral particles during froth flotation.
A furnace lined with Haematite is used to convert cast iron to wrought iron.
questions.chapter: Old syllabus: General Principles and Processes of Isolation of Elements
questions.explanation: Collectors (like pine oil) enhance the non-wettability (hydrophobicity) of the desired mineral particles so they adhere to froth, not their wettability; so statement (3) is incorrect as written.

questions.q: A solution of 1.25 g of 'P' in 50 g of water lowers freezing point by 0.3 °C. Molar mass of 'P' is 94. K$_{f(water)}$ = 1.86 K kg mol$^{-1}$. The degree of association of 'P' in water is
questions.explanation: Calculated ΔT$_f$ (i=1) = 1.86×1000×1.25/(94×50) = 0.495 °C; van't Hoff factor i = 0.3/0.495 = 0.606. For dimerisation, i = 1 - α/2, giving α ≈ 0.787 (≈79%), closest to 80%. KEA awarded a grace mark for this question.

questions.q: Volume occupied by single CsCl ion pair in a crystal is 7.014 × 10$^{-23}$ cm$^3$. The smallest Cs – Cs internuclear distance is equal to length of the side of the cube corresponding to volume of one CsCl ion pair. The smallest Cs to Cs internuclear distance is nearly

For Cr$_2$O$_7^{-2}$ + 14H$^+$ + 6e$^-$ $\rightarrow$ 2Cr$^{+3}$ + 7H$_2$O; E° = 1.33 V At [Cr$_2$O$_7^{-2}$] = 4.5 millimole, [Cr$^{+3}$] = 15 millimole, E is 1.067 V. The pH of the solution is nearly equal to
questions.explanation: Using the Nernst equation E = E° - (0.059/6)log([Cr$^{3+}$]$^2$/([Cr$_2$O$_7^{2-}$][H$^+$]$^{14}$)), solving for [H$^+$] with the given concentrations and potentials gives a pH close to 2.

questions.q: 1.78 g of an optically active L-amino acid (A) is treated with NaNO$_2$/HCl at 0 °C. 448 cm$^3$ of nitrogen was at STP is evolved. A sample of protein has 0.25% of this amino acid by mass. The molar mass of the protein is
questions.explanation: Moles N$_2$ = 448/22400 = 0.02 mol = moles amino acid (1:1 stoichiometry in diazotization); molar mass of amino acid = 1.78/0.02 = 89 g/mol (alanine). If 0.25% of protein mass is this amino acid, minimum molar mass of protein = 89×(100/0.25) = 35,600 g/mol. KEA awarded a grace mark for this question.

questions.q:
10 g of a mixture of BaO and CaO requires 100 cm$^3$ of 2.5 M HCl to react completely. The percentage of calcium oxide in the mixture is approximately

(Given: molar mass of BaO = 153)
questions.explanation: Let x g BaO and (10-x) g CaO; moles HCl = 0.1×2.5 = 0.25 mol; equivalents: 2(x/153) + 2((10-x)/56) = 0.25; solving gives x ≈ 4.74 g BaO, so CaO ≈ 5.26 g, i.e. ≈ 52.6% CaO.

questions.q:
The ratio of heats liberated at 298 K from the combustion of one kg of coke and by burning water gas obtained from kg of coke is

(Assume coke to be 100% carbon.)

(Given enthalpies of combustion of C to CO$_2$, CO to CO$_2$ and H$_2$ to H$_2$O as 393.5 kJ, 285 kJ, 285 kJ respectively all at 298 K.)
questions.explanation: Per mole of carbon, direct combustion releases 393.5 kJ, while water gas (1 mol CO + 1 mol H$_2$) on combustion releases 285+285 = 570 kJ; ratio = 393.5/570 ≈ 0.69:1. KEA awarded a grace mark, likely due to ambiguity in the printed enthalpy values.

questions.q:
Impure copper containing Fe, Au, Ag as impurities is electrolytically refined. A current of 140 A for 482.5 s decreased the mass of the anode by 22.26 g and increased the mass of cathode by 22.011 g. Percentage of iron in impure copper is

(Given molar mass Fe = 55.5 g mol$^{-1}$, molar mass Cu = 63.54 g mol$^{-1}$)
questions.explanation: Total charge = 140×482.5 = 67550 C; charge used to deposit 22.011 g Cu at the cathode = (22.011/63.54)×2×96500 ≈ 66863 C; remaining charge (≈687 C) dissolved Fe from the anode, giving mass Fe ≈ 0.198 g, so %Fe = 0.198/22.26×100 ≈ 0.90%. KEA awarded a grace mark for this question.

questions.q: 25 cm$^3$ of oxalic acid completely neutralised 0.064 g of sodium hydroxide. Molarity of the oxalic acid solution is
questions.explanation: Moles NaOH = 0.064/40 = 0.0016 mol; oxalic acid (diprotic) needs 2 mol NaOH per mol acid, so moles acid = 0.0008 mol; molarity = 0.0008/0.025 = 0.032 M.

questions.q: The statement that is NOT correct is
options: The radius of the first orbit of He$^+$ is half that of the first orbit of hydrogen atom.
Total number of nodes for 3s orbital is three.
Energies of stationary states in hydrogen like atoms is inversely proportional to the square of the principal quantum number.
Angular quantum number signifies the shape of the orbital.
questions.explanation: The 3s orbital has (n-1) = 2 total nodes, not three (2 radial nodes, 0 angular nodes), so statement (2) is incorrect.

questions.q:
For the equilibrium: CaCO$_{3(s)}$ $\rightleftharpoons$ CaO$_{(s)}$ + CO$_{2(g)}$; K$_p$ = 1.64 atm at 1000 K

50 g of CaCO$_3$ in a 10 litre closed vessel is heated to 1000 K. Percentage of CaCO$_3$ that remains unreacted at equilibrium is

(Given R = 0.082 L atm K$^{-1}$ mol$^{-1}$)
questions.explanation: K$_p$ = P(CO$_2$) = 1.64 atm; moles CO$_2$ at equilibrium = PV/RT = 1.64×10/(0.082×1000) = 0.2 mol = moles CaCO$_3$ decomposed (20 g); initial moles CaCO$_3$ = 50/100 = 0.5 mol, so 0.2 mol reacted means 0.3 mol (60%) remains unreacted.

questions.q: Conversion of oxygen into ozone is non-spontaneous at
questions.explanation: 3O$_2$ → 2O$_3$ has positive ΔH (endothermic) and negative ΔS (decrease in moles of gas), so ΔG = ΔH - TΔS is positive at all temperatures, making the conversion non-spontaneous at all temperatures.

questions.q: Density of carbon monoxide is maximum at
questions.explanation: Density ∝ P/T for an ideal gas; comparing P/T ratios: (1) 4/500=0.008, (2) 6/1092≈0.0055, (3) 0.5/273≈0.0018, (4) 2/600≈0.0033 — option (1) has the highest P/T ratio, giving maximum density.

questions.q:
The acid strength of active methylene group in

(a) CH$_3$COCH$_2$COOC$_2$H$_5$

(b) CH$_3$COCH$_2$COCH$_3$

(c) C$_2$H$_5$OOCCH$_2$COOC$_2$H$_5$ decreases as
questions.explanation: Diketone (b, CH$_3$COCH$_2$COCH$_3$) with two strongly electron-withdrawing carbonyl groups is most acidic, keto-ester (a, CH$_3$COCH$_2$COOC$_2$H$_5$) is intermediate, and diester (c, C$_2$H$_5$OOCCH$_2$COOC$_2$H$_5$) with two weaker-withdrawing ester groups is least acidic; so acid strength decreases as b > a > c.

questions.q: A metallic oxide reacts with water to form its hydroxide, hydrogen peroxide and also liberates oxygen. The metallic oxide could be
questions.explanation: Na$_2$O$_2$ (sodium peroxide) reacts with water to give NaOH and H$_2$O$_2$, which partly decomposes to release O$_2$; KO$_2$ (potassium superoxide) reacts with water to give KOH, H$_2$O$_2$, and O$_2$ directly. Both A and C fit the description.

questions.q:
X $\xrightarrow[(Reductive)]{Ozonolysis}$ Y + Z

Y can be obtained by Etard's reaction, Z undergoes disproportionation reaction with concentrated alkali. X could be

[four substituted styrenes: (1) C$_6$H$_5$-CH=C(CH$_3$)$_2$, (2) C$_6$H$_5$-CH=CH-CH$_3$, (3) C$_6$H$_5$-CH=CH$_2$, (4) C$_6$H$_5$-C≡CH]
questions.explanation: Etard's reaction converts toluene to benzaldehyde (Y); reductive ozonolysis of styrene (C$_6$H$_5$-CH=CH$_2$) gives benzaldehyde (Y) and formaldehyde (Z), and formaldehyde undergoes the Cannizzaro (disproportionation) reaction with concentrated alkali.

questions.q: Gold Sol is not
questions.explanation: Gold sol is a multimolecular, lyophobic, negatively charged colloid, but it is not a macromolecular colloid (which consists of large single molecules like proteins or polymers).

questions.q: Carbocation as an intermediate is likely to be formed in the reaction:
questions.chapter: Organic Chemistry: Basic Principles and Techniques
questions.explanation: The acid-catalysed isomerisation of hexane to 2-methylpentane with anhydrous AlCl$_3$/HCl proceeds via a carbocation intermediate; the other reactions proceed by S$_N$2 substitution, nucleophilic addition, and free-radical mechanisms respectively. KEA awarded a grace mark for this question.

questions.q: For an ideal binary liquid mixture
questions.explanation: For an ideal binary liquid mixture, ΔH$_{mix}$ = 0 and ΔV$_{mix}$ = 0, while mixing is spontaneous so ΔS$_{mix}$ > 0 and ΔG$_{mix}$ < 0.

questions.q:
For hydrogen – oxygen fuel cell at one atm and 298 K

H$_{2(g)}$ + $\dfrac{1}{2}$O$_{2(g)}$ $\longrightarrow$ H$_2$O$_{(l)}$; ΔG° = –240 kJ

E° for the cell is approximately,

(Given F = 96,500 C)
Which one of these is not known?
questions.explanation: CuI$_2$ is not known/stable because I$^-$ (a strong reducing agent) reduces Cu$^{2+}$ to Cu$^+$, forming CuI + I$_2$ instead; CuBr$_2$, CuF$_2$ and CuCl$_2$ are all known, stable compounds.

questions.q: The correct statement is
options: Ce$^{+4}$ in aqueous solution is not known.
In general, lanthanoids and actinoids do not show variable oxidation states.
The extent of actinoid contraction is almost the same as lanthanoid contraction.
The earlier members of lanthanoid series resemble calcium in their chemical properties.
questions.explanation: The earlier lanthanoids (La, Ce etc.) are similar in size and chemical behaviour to Ca$^{2+}$/Ca-group elements due to comparable ionic radii, making statement (4) correct; Ce$^{4+}$ is a known stable oxidation state in aqueous solution, and actinoid contraction is greater per element than lanthanoid contraction.

questions.q:
P $\xrightarrow[2. H_3O^+]{1. CH_3MgBr}$ R $\xrightarrow[2. \Delta]{1. dil.\ NaOH}$ 4-methylpent-3-en-2-one

P is
questions.explanation: 4-Methylpent-3-en-2-one is formed by aldol condensation of two acetone molecules; R (the aldol product before dehydration) is 4-hydroxy-4-methylpentan-2-one, which comes from acetone reacting with CH$_3$MgBr followed by hydrolysis of the resulting imine/nitrile addition product — P is ethanenitrile (CH$_3$CN), which with CH$_3$MgBr and hydrolysis gives acetone (R's precursor).

questions.q: When CH$_2$=CH-O-CH$_2$-CH$_3$ reacts with one mole of HI, one of the products formed is
questions.explanation: Vinyl ethyl ether undergoes acid-catalysed addition/cleavage with HI via an oxocarbenium intermediate, breaking down to give ethanal (CH$_3$CHO) and ethyl iodide. KEA awarded a grace mark for this question.

questions.q: 0.44 g of a monohydric alcohol when added to methylmagnesium iodide in ether liberates at S.T.P., 112 cm$^3$ of methane. With PCC the same alcohol forms a carbonyl compound that answers silver mirror test. The monohydric alcohol is
questions.explanation: Moles CH$_4$ = 112/22400 = 0.005 mol = moles alcohol (1:1 with CH$_3$MgI, active H), so molar mass = 0.44/0.005 = 88 g/mol, matching (CH$_3$)$_3$C-CH$_2$OH (neopentyl alcohol, MW 88); being a primary alcohol, PCC oxidises it to an aldehyde which gives a positive silver mirror (Tollens') test.

questions.q:
CH$_3$CH$_2$CH(CH$_3$)-CHO + CH$_3$MgBr $\xrightarrow{ether}$ 'A' $\xrightarrow{H_3O^+}$ B

The IUPAC name of 'B' is
questions.explanation: 2-Methylbutanal + CH$_3$MgBr adds CH$_3$ to the carbonyl carbon, giving a secondary alcohol CH$_3$-CH(OH)-CH(CH$_3$)-CH$_2$CH$_3$... on renumbering for lowest locants this is named 3-methylbutan-2-ol.

questions.q: For Freundlich isotherm a graph of log $\dfrac{x}{m}$ is plotted against log P. The slope of the line and its y-axis intercept, respectively corresponds to
questions.explanation: The Freundlich isotherm equation log(x/m) = log k + (1/n)log P is a straight line with slope 1/n and y-intercept log k.

questions.q:
A plot of $\dfrac{1}{T}$ Vs. ln k for a reaction gives the slope –1 × 10$^4$ K. The energy of activation for the reaction is

(Given R = 8.314 J K$^{-1}$ mol$^{-1}$)
questions.explanation: From the Arrhenius equation, slope = -E$_a$/R, so E$_a$ = -slope×R = 1×10$^4$×8.314 = 83140 J/mol = 83.14 kJ/mol. KEA awarded a grace mark for this question.

questions.q: The IUPAC name of the complex ion formed when gold dissolves in aquaregia is
questions.explanation: Gold dissolves in aqua regia to form the complex ion [AuCl$_4$]$^-$, in which gold is in the +3 oxidation state, named tetrachloridoaurate(III).

questions.q: The correct sequence of reactions to be performed to convert benzene into m-bromoaniline is
questions.explanation: Nitration of benzene gives nitrobenzene (a meta director), which directs bromination to the meta position giving m-bromonitrobenzene, and finally reduction of the nitro group gives m-bromoaniline.
